A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DMLE research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments comparing DMLE with IMLE, a Farquhar et al. comparison, sensitivity analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds dependency-approximation comparisons and per-cycle loss-processing measurements.

M1.justification: The DMLE objective, Algorithm 1 steps, and default Softmax approximation for Top-k selection remain unchanged. V2 clarifies reevaluation under current model parameters and tests alternative approximations without revising the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight classification datasets and retain the illustrative synthetic example. The added approximation and timing analyses reuse existing datasets and task conditions.

E2.justification: Appendix I newly compares the default Softmax dependency approximation against Power and Soft-rank approximations while holding Top-k selection fixed. IMLE and the Farquhar et al. statistical bias-mitigation baseline remain unchanged in the existing comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds an evaluation holding Top-k selection fixed while varying the dependency approximation, using k=1 for MNIST, Iris, and Reuters and k=5 for Tiny ImageNet. It also adds loss-processing timing over 500 MNIST cycles with k=1. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds a dedicated four-dataset ablation addressing the previously untested choice of dependency approximation under Top-k selection. Appendix E also adds per-cycle loss-cost analysis beyond aggregate runtime measurements. Together these substantially extend diagnostics of approximation choice and computational overhead.

E5.justification: Both versions specify eight random seeds, report accuracy means with one standard deviation, and use Wilcoxon signed-rank testing at p<0.05. The new approximation plots follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no revised statistical procedure or increased run count is stated.

E6.justification: New Figures 7 and 10 report growing loss-processing costs, with greater overhead for DMLE, and approximation comparisons favoring Softmax. All entries in the retained entropy, BALD, least-confidence, and total-runtime tables match across versions. The additions are supporting results, not improved scores in the original comparisons.

T1.justification: The likelihood derivations, Theorems 1–2, and proofs in Appendices A–C are unchanged. The new glossary restates existing notation, and the added conceptual discussion introduces no new formal result.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same contributions: accounting for sample dependencies during parameter estimation and improving active-learning performance over IMLE. The abstract's reported average accuracy improvements of 6%, 8.6%, and 10.5% are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explains the shared parameter governing prediction and selection, motivates Softmax through computational simplicity, and discusses growing per-cycle overhead. The conclusion identifies unresolved theoretical characterization of the Top-k approximation and conditions where benefits might diminish.

D1.justification: V2 newly states that the implementation is publicly available and provides a GitHub access link in the abstract. The existing framework, optimizer, learning rate, hardware, and dataset-source disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Raginsky and Rakhlin (2011) and Lattimore and Szepesvári (2019) to distinguish its treatment of model-dependent selection. Golovin and Krause (2017) motivates future submodular optimization work. The broader related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds localized explanations, expands future-work discussion, introduces a glossary, and swaps the timing and additional-results appendices. Most prose and the main section structure remain intact, with smaller edits to author names, publication information, and Algorithm 1's title.

P2.justification: V2 adds the timing plot, four-panel approximation figure, and glossary table. Figure 2 moves into Background, and existing tables and appendix figures are relocated or renumbered. Original figure content and numerical table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 provides direct empirical support for the previously untested Top-k approximation choice and clarifies computational overhead through per-cycle measurements. The code-access information, glossary, and more explicit open questions also improve usability. These are focused gains: the method, proofs, and main benchmark results remain unchanged, and theoretical justification of the Top-k approximation remains future work.
